content.title: About
content.content: Yeast extract spread is a concentrated product made from autolyzed cells of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. It has a strong umami flavor, with a slightly salty and mildly sweet note, and is often used as a flavor enhancer, cheese substitute, or sauce base.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Commercial production of yeast extract began in the early 20th century in Japan under the brand “Miso”.
It is rich in B‑vitamins, especially B12, which is rare in plant‑based foods.
The spread is popular in vegetarian and vegan cuisine as a cheese‑like flavor enhancer.
High glutamic acid content provides natural umami without added MSG.
In some countries it is classified as a food additive, in others as a ready‑to‑eat product.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast extract contains thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, vitamin B6 and folate, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: About 10 g of plant protein are present per 100 g of spread, making it a useful addition to vegetarian diets.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans in yeast can stimulate immune cells and improve resistance to infections.

items.title: Enhances flavor with less salt
items.content: The umami taste allows reduction of added salt in dishes, beneficial for blood‑pressure management.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Autolysis partially breaks down yeast cells, making the nutrients more readily absorbable.

items.title: Yeast allergy
items.content: People allergic to yeast or fermented products may experience skin rash, swelling, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Some spreads contain up to 1 g of sodium per 100 g, so individuals monitoring salt intake should limit portions.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Yeast extract is high in purines, which can be problematic for gout or hyperuricemia sufferers.

items.title: Glutamate sensitivity
items.content: Although glutamate is natural, sensitive individuals may experience headaches or a tingling sensation after large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread can be used on bread, mixed into sauces, soups, marinades, vegan “cheese” dishes, or added to smoothies for a flavor boost. Keep refrigerated and stir before use, as oil may separate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the spread in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Shelf life is typically 12 months after opening. Discard if the smell, color, or texture changes or if mold appears.
